purpose.summary: Turn the default-off local-regtest Chronik block observer into a bounded, restart- and full-reindex-reconstructible active-chain projection without adding persistence or consensus authority.
scope: Ask one falsifiable question: can public canonical block inputs reconstruct and reverse an exact 288-block active-chain suffix across normal restart, full reindex, and deep reorganization while the observer remains optional and non-authoritative?

Pass canonical CBlock serialization through the existing synchronous C ABI, own the bytes in Rust, and independently verify callback identity, exact deserialization, non-empty transactions, and the header Merkle root.
Track only block identity, height, and transaction count with exact parent-plus-height connects, exact LIFO disconnects, checked arithmetic, and a hard MIN_BLOCKS_TO_KEEP bound of 288.

At normal startup, reconstruct the readable active suffix in a distinct staging observer and atomically adopt it only after every block passes; during full -reindex, rebuild from ordered validation callbacks starting at genesis.
When a reorganization disconnects the retained anchor, enter one explicit observer-only rebuild-required state, reject subsequent observer events, and recover through a normal restart bootstrap.

Prove disabled legacy mining, enabled local-regtest behavior, an actual height-288 full reindex, the retention bound, deep-reorganization failure, restart recovery, exact non-regtest rejection, and no Chronik file or socket.
exclusions: No persistent index, database, migration, resume marker, file, socket, API, service, Rust thread, or query surface is added.
No mempool event or transaction-output classification is added; SLP, ALP, and CashTokens families remain unrecognized by the node observer.
No authoritative token validation, token state, or governed native-asset activation is implemented.
No callback result can accept, reject, reorder, or select a block, transaction, or chain; observer failure affects only explicit local-regtest observer startup or projection state.
No consensus, chain parameter, activation, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, or user-interface behavior changes.
No local binary, build cache, raw output, absolute host path, parent environment, operator material, private history, or unrelated product material enters this change.

commands: Fresh-configure and build bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_BUILD_ONLY=OFF and BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF, then run symbol, option, and mining_basic checks.
expected_results: CMake does not enter Chronik, no observer symbol or option exists, -chronikobserver is rejected as unknown, and legacy mining passes.

commands: Fresh-configure and build bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON, inspect the final executable, launch without -chronikobserver, and run mining_basic.
expected_results: The executable contains all six governed Rust C-ABI symbols; runtime launches register no observer or Chronik state by default; legacy mining passes.

commands: Run feature_chronik_block_observer.py --hermetic-child-env against the compiled-in build on a fresh isolated regtest datadir.
expected_results: The bounded volatile active-chain projection passes opt-in, restart, height-288 full-reindex, retention, and deep-reorganization scenarios without creating an authoritative or durable index.

scenarios.command: Run feature_chronik_block_observer.py: first runtime disabled, then explicit local-regtest opt-in with bootstrap, connect, disconnect, reconsider, and exact non-regtest rejection probes.
expected_results: Disabled execution emits no Chronik state; enabled local regtest reconstructs its initial suffix, emits the exact six-event reversible sequence and payload-derived totals, creates no Chronik path or socket, and main, testnet, testnet4, and scalenet reject opt-in.
failure_conditions: Any enabled non-regtest launch, callback or payload mismatch, state while disabled, Chronik path/socket, validation decision, or activation claim fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: After reaching height 288 and forcing the bounded projection into rebuild-required state, start a fresh opt-in process on the unchanged datadir and then mine height 289.
expected_results: Startup atomically reconstructs exactly heights 1 through 288 with 288 blocks and 288 transactions; the next block advances to height 289 while retaining exactly 288 entries.
failure_conditions: Failure to reconstruct the exact available suffix, totals other than 288, stale rebuild-required state, non-atomic partial adoption, or growth beyond 288 fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: With an existing active chain at height 288, launch a fresh opt-in process with -reindex=1 and wait for the validation-interface queue to drain.
expected_results: Bootstrap reports an empty active chain, full reindex emits exact ordered connects for genesis through height 288, and the projection remains bounded to the most recent 288 blocks and transactions.
failure_conditions: Missing, duplicated, reordered, or rejected reindex callbacks; an incorrect block identity, height, payload, Merkle root, total, or bound; or use of prior volatile state fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: After full reindex at height 288, invalidate the retained height-1 anchor, drain callbacks, reconsider it while failed closed, then restart normally.
expected_results: Exactly 288 LIFO disconnects end at sequence 577, one retained-anchor-disconnected diagnostic requires restart, reconsidered connects are rejected by the observer, and normal restart reconstructs the active suffix.
failure_conditions: Mutation after rebuild-required, more than one transition diagnostic, acceptance of a non-LIFO disconnect, silent continuation past the anchor, node consensus influence, or failure to recover on restart fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: The projection is volatile and non-queryable; it stores no durable index, transaction body, output classification, or API state.
Normal startup reconstruction is synchronous and fails the explicit local-regtest observer startup if any selected retained block cannot be read or parsed.
Peak parsing memory includes C++ serialization, one Rust-owned block buffer, and parsed transaction structures; only compact metadata for at most 288 blocks is retained.
Dedicated -reindex-chainstate and actually pruned-datadir canaries are not implemented in this change.

The local macOS final binaries required an untracked Boost 1.90 compatibility include because unchanged legacy code calls removed boost::filesystem::basename; those binaries are diagnostic only and never evidence artifacts.
The committed lockfile fixes registry versions and checksums but does not lock the compiler, operating-system image, native toolchain, or final binaries.
A fresh Cargo cache requires one online population step before governed offline builds.
Local tests are contradiction checks only; no result is public reproduction evidence at record-review time.
counterevidence: No public build or functional execution of the exact candidate exists at record-review time.
A bounded volatile projection does not demonstrate durable indexing, crash recovery, API compatibility, mempool reconstruction, native-asset parsing, token validity, or consensus behavior.
The distinct index-chainstate-reindex-288 and index-pruned-datadir-288 scenarios remain deliberately unimplemented and Open Question.
Local success on macOS does not establish Ubuntu, cross-platform, or independently reproduced behavior.
